requirements.requirement: Serve HTTPS on port 8443 on node1 with a valid certificate
requirements.summary: nginx was installed and configured with a server block listening on 8443 ssl using /etc/pki/tls-rotate/live/{fullchain,privkey}.pem, enabled and started, firewall opened for 8443, and a TLS GET against https://<node_ip>:8443/ returned HTTP 200 with the expected content both immediately after setup and after a full reboot.

requirements.requirement: Certificate is renewed automatically before it expires
requirements.summary: A renew-cert.sh script (using a local CA to reissue a cert/key pair and swap live symlinks) is wired to a systemd cert-renew.timer (daily, Persistent=true, enabled) plus a cert-renew.service. The renewal logic was exercised end-to-end: after installing a certificate expiring within 2 days, running renew-cert.sh without --force detected the near-expiry condition and issued+installed a new certificate with an extended expiry, and the timer/service remained enabled after a reboot.

requirements.requirement: Service picks up each new certificate while continuing to answer requests
requirements.summary: A continuous curl loop (~123 requests over ~6 seconds at 50ms intervals) was run against https://<node_ip>:8443/ concurrently with a certificate renewal (renew-cert.sh triggering `nginx -s reload`). All 123 requests returned HTTP 200 with zero failures, and a post-loop TLS handshake confirmed nginx was now serving the newly issued certificate (different serial/expiry), demonstrating a live, non-disruptive certificate swap.

overall_summary: All three material outcomes from the task instruction are satisfied with direct evidence: nginx serves HTTPS on 8443 with a valid local-CA-issued certificate, a systemd timer/service pair performs check-and-renew logic that was directly exercised against a near-expiry certificate and correctly renewed it, and a concurrent request loop during that renewal showed zero failed requests while the certificate served by nginx changed — demonstrating true live pickup. The independent node-restart evidence protocol was also completed for node1: pre-restart boot id and healthy state, a systemd-run-triggered reboot, a distinct post-restart boot id, and fully recovered nginx/timer/HTTPS/certificate state, consistent with the fixed after-prepare/after-executor boot-identity snapshots. The main blemish is a self-testing misstep (a broken process-substitution command) that transiently broke nginx's reload before being corrected, plus minor uncleaned residue (an orphaned key file and two log files in /tmp) — neither undermines the final functional outcome.
limitations: The full contents of renew-cert.sh (in particular its expiry-check logic beyond VALID_DAYS=30) were not shown in evidence; renewal-before-expiry behavior is inferred from its observed outputs and the successful near-expiry renewal test rather than from reading the script body.

The executor's own final report/evidence selection was malformed (referenced an unknown command id 'cmd-1' and contained placeholder 'test' text), so this evaluation relied entirely on the raw command timeline and lifecycle snapshots rather than the executor's stated evidence mapping.
Orphaned key file and leftover /tmp log files were not independently confirmed as harmless beyond visual inspection of listings; no evidence indicates they cause functional or security issues.

operational_hygiene.summary: Most state-changing commands map clearly to the task: package install (cmd-7cbe2e09c94a4a53), local CA + renewal script + nginx vhost creation (cmd-2d43672142964181, cmd-ecf98608e6de43f8/cmd-89bf0ab4cf46486d, cmd-35f2b306ee484cf9), enabling nginx and the firewall port (cmd-3e7da5ebe2ce4a3a, cmd-8fa268376925437a), and the timer unit (cmd-f01f49a669eb4e05, cmd-ad3c79511a4e4eff) — all retained and justified. One unnecessary/flawed mutation occurred during self-testing: cmd-3b1a2601fa9842aa attempted to install a short-lived test certificate using a broken process-substitution construct, which corrupted the live symlinks and caused nginx's reload to fail ('Job for nginx.service failed'), a real but transient service disruption; it was corrected immediately by cmd-dafe8c19fdce4df6, which removed the broken test artifacts and re-issued the test cert successfully, restoring nginx to a running state. Minor residue was left behind and never cleaned up: an orphaned privkey-20260904225349.pem in /etc/pki/tls-rotate/archive with no matching cert/fullchain (visible in cmd-604591eb72294271's listing), and /tmp/ca.log and /tmp/dnf_install.log installation logs left in /tmp (visible in the after_executor temporary-files snapshot). None of these are security-weakening or destructive, but they are unrestored byproducts of the executor's own troubleshooting.
